name: Muse Code
tagline: Meta's terminal coding agent — pay standard rate and it never trains on your code, or opt into Contributor pricing for a steep discount if you let it.
verdict: Muse Code is a capable, fast-following terminal coding agent from a company with the compute and model budget to make Claude Code and Codex CLI defend their pricing, not yet a reason to switch tools outright. Its one genuinely novel mechanic is priced, not just toggled: a Contributor tier bills roughly 8-12x less per token than Standard in exchange for letting Meta train future models on your prompts and completions, a direct price-for-data trade neither Claude Code nor Codex CLI offers, both only ship an opt-out toggle at a fixed price either way. The parallel sub-agent worktree model is a real capability edge for large, multi-part jobs, but it launched three days before this listing was researched, as a beta, with no independent benchmark yet and no dedicated IDE or GUI surface. Pick it to evaluate Meta's own coding model at a real cost discount or to trial multi-worktree parallelism on a big refactor; look elsewhere for an established daily driver with outside-verified accuracy.
